value.rationale: The target-current cospectrum is a natural experimental observable in burst-fed reaction–diffusion systems. It is surprising that strictly nonnegative correlations at every time lag can have infinitely many negative-frequency cospectral bands for every noncentral source but never at the midpoint. The sharp spectral root sequence identifies the geometrical source displacement and independent mortality rate without burst calibration, a nontrivial structural dichotomy and inverse consequence. The exact high-frequency result is explicitly distinguished from finite-noise feasible estimation.
